source_text: Si quis dicit mutabilem aut alterabilem Christum, et non confitetur ipsum immutabilem spiritu, corruptibilem carne; anathema sit. Qua ratione potest aliquis dicere, mutabilem aut variabilem esse Christum? cum ipse Dominus dicat: Ego sum, et non mutor. Et rursum: Neque anima eius relicta est in inferno; neque caro eius vidit corruptionem.
thought_title: Christ Unchangeable in Spirit Yet Corruptible in Flesh
orientation: Gregory condemns the claim that Christ is changeable, affirming that Christ is truly God and truly man.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says changeable or alterable Christ, and not confesses him unchangeable [in] spirit, corruptible [in] flesh; anathema be. [by] what reason can anyone say, changeable or variable [to] be Christ? since himself Lord says: I am, and not I change. And again: nor soul his left was in hell; nor flesh his saw corruption.

choices.why: keeps the two different Latin adjectives distinct instead of merging them

choices.english: unchangeable in spirit and corruptible in flesh
choices.why: preserves the contrasted ablatives and uses the brief glossary rendering flesh for caro
rejected: immutable in spirit, corruptible in body

choices.english: By what reason can anyone say
choices.why: keeps the rhetorical question force that denies any reason for the claim

choices.english: I am, and I do not change
choices.why: keeps present tense and first person agency of the cited speech
rejected: I am he and am unchanging

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ is changeable or alterable, and does not confess him unchangeable in spirit and corruptible in flesh, let him be anathema. By what reason can anyone say that Christ is changeable or variable? For the Lord himself says: “I am, and I do not change” (Malachi 3:6). And again: “His soul was not left in hell, nor did his flesh see corruption” (Acts 2:31).
